PKG-002.what_the_fix_does: Swaps two ADJACENT standalone lines \usepackage[..]{hyperref} / \usepackage[..]{geometry} (whitespace-only between them, not in verbatim or comment), so geometry loads before hyperref.
PKG-002.examples: Real sample 2507.10114: '\usepackage{hyperref}\n\usepackage{geometry}' swapped, 0 hunks. MEASURED synthetic: hyperref[colorlinks,pdfpagelayout=...] and geometry[a5paper,margin=1cm] swapped, rc 0 on both sides with 0 text diff.
PKG-002.rationale: It only reorders two adjacent, single-package, standalone preamble lines. geometry and hyperref do not depend on each other's load order for page content (hyperref reads the page size at \begin{document}). The strict adjacency and standalone preconditions exclude interleaved configuration. INFERRED: no case found where it changes typeset content.

refutation.evidence:
MEASURED, reproducible. Three minimal cases in /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-dylanpossamai-Library-CloudStorage-Dropbox-Work-Articles-Scripts/6724887f-375f-4639-96cf-722343631c21/scratchpad/pkg002/{e1,e2,e3}, harness h.py in the same directory. Each was built pristine and with LP_FIX_ONLY=PKG-002 --apply-fixes, compiled with run_to_fixpoint (rc 0 both ways), and compared with pdftotext. In all three the fix changes LaTeX source code that the paper prints as content.

(e2) main.tex does \input{recipe}. recipe.tex says "A minimal example of the misordering our tool reports:" followed by \begin{verbatim*}\n\usepackage{hyperref}\n\usepackage{geometry}\n\end{verbatim*}. Trace: `1 PKG-002 73 116 "\usepackage{geometry}\n\usepackage{hyperref}"`. PDF before: hyperref, then geometry. PDF after: geometry, then hyperref. The paper's example of the WRONG order now shows the correct order, so its sentence now describes a listing that contradicts it.

(e1) Same shape using fancyvrb's \begin{Verbatim}[frame=single] in an \input'd section file ("Our template loads the packages in exactly this order ... reproduce verbatim"). The printed lines are swapped in the same way.

(e3) Single-file case with no subfile. The preamble has \begin{filecontents*}[overwrite]{example.tex} holding the two lines, and the body shows them with \lstinputlisting{example.tex}. The fix (offsets 70-113 of main.tex) rewrites the file contents, so the listed "bug report" preamble is reordered in the PDF.

Root cause, read from the source:
- The fix edits whatever it finds in "the preamble", but `extract_preamble` (validators_common.ml:2571) returns the WHOLE FILE when there is no \begin{document}. That is true of every \input/\include'd section file.
- `find_verbatim_comment_ranges` (validators_common.ml:2470) protects only exact `verbatim`, `lstlisting` and `minted` bodies plus % comments. `verbatim*`, fancyvrb `Verbatim`, `filecontents`/`filecontents*`, custom lstnewenvironment envs, tcblisting and the `comment` env are all unprotected.
- So `reorder_pkg_swap_edits` (validators_l2.ml:363) swaps displayed code.

Corpus, MEASURED: 21 files have an adjacent standalone hyperref-then-geometry pair. 15 of them receive the edit. For every one of those 15, pristine and fixed builds give identical pdftotext text, identical per-page pdfinfo sizes and identical 20-dpi page rasters, with no new or lost LaTeX/package warnings. 5 get no edit (diagnose-only); 2507.05774v1 fails to compile with or without the fix. So on real preambles the swap itself looks harmless (the 2507.10114v1 audit result is confirmed). No corpus file has the pair inside a listing: MEASURED absence in this corpus only. The damage appears only when the pair is shown as code, which is realistic for LaTeX-tooling or tutorial papers.

SPC-027.what_the_fix_does: Deletes leading and trailing spaces/tabs inside \url{...} (not inside verbatim or comments).
SPC-027.examples: Real sample 2507.10209: '\url{ https://github.com/...}' -> leading space removed, 0 hunks. MEASURED synthetic with url[obeyspaces]: '\url{<TAB>http://b.org}' originally printed a garbage 'Ψ' glyph for the tab and after the fix prints 'http://b.org'. '\url{ https://a.org/x y }' is trimmed only at the ends, and the interior space is kept.
SPC-027.rationale: The whitespace it removes is either ignored by url.sty (default) or, under obeyspaces, is spurious output that no author wants. It also cleans the hyperlink target. The regex needs a literal '\url{', so \burl and \nolinkurl are not touched. No hazard found.

refutation.evidence:
The claim is REFUTED, but only with synthetic documents. No real paper in the corpus triggers the damage.

MEASURED on the corpus. A Python replica of the producer regex `\url{([^}]*)}` over every .tex file in the 2961 corpus packages finds 9 sites: 6 live, in 5 papers, and 3 inside comments. I ran all 5 papers pristine and with `LP_FIX_ONLY=SPC-027 --apply-fixes`, with a fresh copy for each build and `run_to_fixpoint`:
- 2506.20533v2, 2507.10209v1, 2506.17838v1, 2507.01055v1 and 2507.11279v1: rc 0 before and after, 7 edits in total, the same page counts, 0 pdftotext word hunks and 0 changed `-layout` lines.
So on real papers the fix is invisible in the text.

MEASURED on minimal article documents that load fancyvrb, listings, alltt and hyperref. Every one compiles to rc 0 both before and after the fix. `LP_FIX_TRACE` shows 2 SPC-027 deletions per document (the leading and trailing space), and each one changes the typeset code shown in the output:
1. `\begin{verbatim*}` containing `\url{ http://x.org }` becomes `\url{http://x.org}`. The word hunk is `\url{␣http://x.org␣}` -> `\url{http://x.org}`, so the visible-space glyphs, which are the whole point of `verbatim*`, are deleted. Trace: `1 SPC-027 148 149 ""` and `1 SPC-027 161 162 ""`. `find_verbatim_comment_ranges` covers only verbatim, lstlisting and minted, and it evidently does not cover `verbatim*`.
2. `\verb|\url{ http://x.org }|`: the hunk is `\url{ http://x.org }` -> `\url{http://x.org}`. Inline `\verb` is not guarded, so the code the author quoted is silently rewritten.
3. `\lstinline|\url{ http://x.org }|`: the same hunk.
4. fancyvrb `\begin{Verbatim}` and `\begin{BVerbatim}`: the same hunk. These environments are not in the guard list.
5. `alltt` (here the pristine output was already garbled by url.sty; the fixed output differs): the hunk is `\unhbox\voidb@x\protect\penalty\@M\http://x.org...` -> `http://x.org`.

MEASURED as correctly safe:
- `lstlisting`: withheld, 0 edits.
- `[obeyspaces,spaces]{url}`: 0 hunks.
- `\url` redefined as `\texttt{#1}`: 0 hunks.
- `\url{\\srv\share\ }` (backslash-space at the end): the fixer made 0 edits, but my test document failed to compile pristine (rc 1), so that case is inconclusive.

INFERRED: realistic exposure is low. Only LaTeX-tutorial or tool papers that quote `\url{ ... }` in `\verb`, `\lstinline` or fancyvrb will hit it, and the corpus has 0 such sites. Even so, the defect is a genuine change to the displayed source-code content. The same class of hole is likely in other producers that rely on `find_verbatim_comment_ranges`. Files are in scratchpad/skep_spc027/ (syn.py, run.py, scan.py and syn/*).
